ukberi-tibyan:1-1.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ اتَّقُوا رَبَّكُمْ إِنَّ زَلْزَلَةَ السَّاعَةِ شَيْءٌ عَظِيمٌ (١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (إِنَّ زَلْزَلَةَ السَّاعَةِ): الزَّلْزَلَةُ is a maṣdar (verbal noun). It may be from the intransitive verb, i.e. "that the Hour's quaking is a thing…" (تَزَلْزَلَ السَّاعَةَ شَيْءٌ) [Translator's note: so vocalized in the source]; or it may be transitive, i.e. "the Hour's making people quake" (إِنَّ زِلْزَالَ السَّاعَةِ النَّاسَ); so in both views the maṣdar is put in construct with its agent. It may also be that the maṣdar is put in construct with the adverb (ẓarf) [Translator's note: i.e. the quaking that occurs at the Hour].

ukberi-tibyan:11-11.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يَعْبُدُ اللَّهَ عَلَى حَرْفٍ فَإِنْ أَصَابَهُ خَيْرٌ اطْمَأَنَّ بِهِ وَإِنْ أَصَابَتْهُ فِتْنَةٌ انْقَلَبَ عَلَى وَجْهِهِ خَسِرَ الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةَ ذَلِكَ هُوَ الْخُسْرَانُ الْمُبِينُ (١١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (عَلَى حَرْفٍ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial); i.e. wavering and unsteady.
(خَسِرَ الدُّنْيَا): it is a ḥāl; i.e. "he turned back, having lost"; and it may be resumptive.
It is also read: خَاسِرَ الدُّنْيَا, and «خَسِرَ الدُّنْيَا» as a noun (خَسِرَ); it too is a ḥāl, and «الْآخِرَةِ» on this reading is in the genitive.

ukberi-tibyan:13-13.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَدْعُو لَمَنْ ضَرُّهُ أَقْرَبُ مِنْ نَفْعِهِ لَبِئْسَ الْمَوْلَى وَلَبِئْسَ الْعَشِيرُ (١٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (يَدْعُو لَمَنْ ضَرُّهُ): this is a place over which the opinions of the grammarians have differed. The reason is that the lām suspends (tuʿalliq) the verb before it from governing when it is one of the verbs of the heart (afʿāl al-qulūb), and يَدْعُو is not one of them. They have two approaches to this. The first: that «يَدْعُو» does not govern what comes after it, neither in wording nor implicitly; on this there are three views. The first of them: that it is a repetition of the first «يَدْعُو», so it has nothing governed by it. The second: that «ذَلِكَ» has the meaning of الَّذِي and is in the position of the accusative governed by يَدْعُو; i.e. "he calls upon that which is error", but the object was placed first. This is according to the view of those who make ذَا, with something other than interrogation, have the meaning of الَّذِي.
The third: that the implied form is "that is the far error, (he) calling upon"; so ذَلِكَ is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and هُوَ is a second mubtadaʾ, or a badal (substitute), or a support (ʿimād, i.e. the separating pronoun); الضَّلَالُ is the khabar (predicate) of the mubtadaʾ, and يَدْعُو is a ḥāl (circumstantial), the implied form being "being called upon" (مَدْعُوًّا). There is weakness in this.
On these views, the speech after it is resumptive: «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ, and the khabar is «لَبِئْسَ الْمَوْلَى».
The second approach: that «يَدْعُو» is connected with what comes after it; on this there are three views. The first: that «يَدْعُو» resembles the verbs of the heart, because its meaning is "he names as a god the one whose harm is nearer than his benefit", and that only issues from a belief, so it is as if He said يَظُنُّ ("he thinks"); and it is better to take its implied form as يَزْعُمُ ("he claims"), because يَزْعُمُ is speech accompanied by belief. The second: that «يَدْعُو» has the meaning of يَقُولُ ("he says"), and «مَنْ» is a mubtadaʾ; «ضَرُّهُ» is a second mubtadaʾ and «أَقْرَبُ» is its khabar; the clause is the ṣila (relative clause) of «مَنْ», and the khabar of مَنْ is omitted, its implied form being "a god" or "my god"; the position of the clause is accusative, governed by the (verb of) saying; and «لَبِئْسَ» is resumptive, because it cannot validly be included in the quoted speech, since the disbelievers do not say of their idols: "evil indeed is the patron".
The third view is the opinion of al-Farrāʾ, namely that the implied form is يَدْعُو مَنْ لَضَرُّهُ ("he calls upon one whose harm, indeed…"); then the lām was moved ahead of its place. This is far-fetched, because what is in the ṣila of الَّذِي does not come before it.

ukberi-tibyan:15-15.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (مَنْ كَانَ يَظُنُّ أَنْ لَنْ يَنْصُرَهُ اللَّهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالْآخِرَةِ فَلْيَمْدُدْ بِسَبَبٍ إِلَى السَّمَاءِ ثُمَّ لْيَقْطَعْ فَلْيَنْظُرْ هَلْ يُذْهِبَنَّ كَيْدُهُ مَا يَغِيظُ (١٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مَنْ كَانَ): it is conditional, and the apodosis (jawāb) is فَلْيَمْدُدْ.
(هَلْ يُذْهِبَنَّ): in the position of the accusative, governed by «يَنْظُرْ».
The majority read kasra on the lām in «لِيَقْطَعْ». It has also been read with it quiescent, by likening «ثُمَّ» to the wāw and the fāʾ, since all of them are conjunctions.

ukberi-tibyan:16-16.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَكَذَلِكَ أَنْزَلْنَاهُ آيَاتٍ بَيِّنَاتٍ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي مَنْ يُرِيدُ (١٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ يَهْدِي): i.e. "and We sent down that Allah guides"; and the implied form is: "mention that Allah…".
The implied form may also be: "and because Allah guides by the signs whom He wills, We sent them down".

ukberi-tibyan:17-17.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَالَّذِينَ هَادُوا وَالصَّابِئِينَ وَالنَّصَارَى وَالْمَجُوسَ وَالَّذِينَ أَشْرَكُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ شَهِيدٌ (١٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا): the khabar (predicate) of «إِنَّ» is the second إِنَّ with its noun and its khabar, namely His saying «إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْصِلُ بَيْنَهُمْ». It is also said: the second «إِنَّ» is a repetition of the first. It is also said: the khabar is omitted, its implied form being "they will be separated on the Day of Resurrection", or the like, and what is mentioned is an explanation of it.

ukberi-tibyan:18-18.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ يَسْجُدُ لَهُ مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ وَمَنْ فِي الْأَرْضِ وَالشَّمْسُ وَالْقَمَرُ وَالنُّجُومُ وَالْجِبَالُ وَالشَّجَرُ وَالدَّوَابُّ وَكَثِيرٌ مِنَ النَّاسِ وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ الْعَذَابُ وَمَنْ يُهِنِ اللَّهُ فَمَا لَهُ مِنْ مُكْرِمٍ إِنَّ اللَّهَ يَفْعَلُ مَا يَشَاءُ (١٨)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَالدَّوَابُّ): it is read with the bāʾ undoubled (الدَّوَابُ); this is far-fetched, because it is from الدَّبِيب ("creeping"). Its justification is that he dropped the first bāʾ out of dislike of the doubling and of the meeting of two quiescent letters.
(كَثِيرٌ): a mubtadaʾ (subject).
(مِنَ النَّاسِ): an adjective (ṣifa) of it, and the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "are obedient", or "are rewarded", or the like.
This is indicated by His saying: (وَكَثِيرٌ حَقَّ عَلَيْهِ الْعَذَابُ), the implied form being "and many of them". It cannot be conjoined to His saying «مَنْ فِي السَّمَاوَاتِ», because people are included in that.
It is also said: it is conjoined to it, and repeated for detailing.
(مِنْ مُكْرِمٍ): with kasra on the rāʾ. It is also read with fatḥa on the rāʾ (مُكْرَمٍ), and it is then a maṣdar (verbal noun) with the meaning of الْإِكْرَام ("honouring").

ukberi-tibyan:19-20.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (هَذَانِ خَصْمَانِ اخْتَصَمُوا فِي رَبِّهِمْ فَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا قُطِّعَتْ لَهُمْ ثِيَابٌ مِنْ نَارٍ يُصَبُّ مِنْ فَوْقِ رُءُوسِهِمُ الْحَمِيمُ (١٩) يُصْهَرُ بِهِ مَا فِي بُطُونِهِمْ وَالْجُلُودُ (٢٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (خَصْمَانِ): it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun) used as an adjective, and the most frequent usage is to keep it singular; whoever puts it in the dual and plural treats it like adjectives and nouns.
(اخْتَصَمُوا): it was made plural only by construing according to the meaning, because each disputing party is a group containing individuals.
His saying, the Exalted: (يُصَبُّ): a resumptive clause. It may also be a second khabar (predicate), or a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the pronoun in «لَهُمْ».
(يُصْهَرُ) with the hāʾ undoubled. It has also been read doubled (يُصَهَّرُ) for intensity; and the clause is a ḥāl from «الْحَمِيمُ».

ukberi-tibyan:2-2.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَوْمَ تَرَوْنَهَا تَذْهَلُ كُلُّ مُرْضِعَةٍ عَمَّا أَرْضَعَتْ وَتَضَعُ كُلُّ ذَاتِ حَمْلٍ حَمْلَهَا وَتَرَى النَّاسَ سُكَارَى وَمَا هُمْ بِسُكَارَى وَلَكِنَّ عَذَابَ اللَّهِ شَدِيدٌ (٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (يَوْمَ تَرَوْنَهَا): it is accusative, governed by «تَذْهَلُ». It may also be a badal (substitute) from السَّاعَة according to the view of whoever makes it indeclinable (mabnī); or an adverb (ẓarf) for عَظِيمٌ; or by implying اذْكُرْ ("mention"). On these views «تَذْهَلُ» is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the object pronoun, and the returning pronoun is omitted; i.e. "forgets in it…". It may not be an adverb for الزَّلْزَلَة, because that is a maṣdar (verbal noun) about which a predication has already been made.
(الْمُرْضِعَةُ): it comes according to the verb; had it come according to relation (nasab, i.e. "one characterized by nursing"), he would have said مُرْضِعٌ.
(مَا): has the meaning of مَنْ; and it may be maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya).
(تَرَى النَّاسَ): the majority read it in the second person, with the agent named.
It is also read with ḍamma on the tāʾ (تُرَى); i.e. "and you are made to see", you who are addressed, or O Muḥammad ﷺ.
It is also read likewise but with «النَّاسُ» in the nominative, with the feminine (verb) according to the meaning of a group.
It is also read with yāʾ; i.e. "and the people see" (وَيَرَى النَّاسُ), i.e. they perceive.
(سُكَارَى): a ḥāl on all the views. Ḍamma and fatḥa in it (سُكَارَى / سَكَارَى) are two dialectal forms, both of which have been read; and سَكْرَى, like مَرْضَى; the singular is سَكْرَانُ, or سَكِرٌ, like زَمِنٌ and زَمْنَى.
It is also read (سُكْرَى), like حُبْلَى. It is said: it is shortened from سُكَارَى; and it is also said: it is a singular like حُبْلَى, as if He said: "you see the community drunk".

ukberi-tibyan:22-22.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كُلَّمَا أَرَادُوا أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا مِنْهَا مِنْ غَمٍّ أُعِيدُوا فِيهَا وَذُوقُوا عَذَابَ الْحَرِيقِ (٢٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (كُلَّمَا): what governs it is «أُعِيدُوا».
«مِنْ غَمٍّ»: a badal (substitute) with repetition of the preposition, a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl). It is also said: the first (مِنْ) is for the beginning of the extent, and the second has the meaning of "because of".
(ذُوقُوا): i.e. "and it was said to them"; so the (verb of) saying was omitted.

ukberi-tibyan:23-23.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُدْخِلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ جَنَّاتٍ تَجْرِي مِنْ تَحْتِهَا الْأَنْهَارُ يُحَلَّوْنَ فِيهَا مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ مِنْ ذَهَبٍ وَلُؤْلُؤًا وَلِبَاسُهُمْ فِيهَا حَرِيرٌ (٢٣)).
His saying, the Exalted: (يُحَلَّوْنَ): it is read with the lām doubled, from التَّحْلِيَة, adorning with ornaments.
It is also read undoubled, from your saying أُحْلِيَ, "he was clothed in ornaments"; and it is from حَلِيَتِ الْمَرْأَةُ تَحْلَى, when the woman wears ornaments. It may also be from حَلِيَ بِعَيْنَيَّ كَذَا, "such-and-such was pleasing in my eyes", when it is beautiful. Then «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida), or the object is omitted.
(مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ): a naʿt (adjective) of it. It is also said: it is from حَلَيْتُ بِكَذَا, "I obtained such-and-such", when I gained it.
(مِنْ ذَهَبٍ): a naʿt of أَسَاوِر.
(وَلُؤْلُؤًا): conjoined to أَسَاوِر, not to ذَهَب, because a bracelet is not usually made of pearl, while it can be an ornament.
It is also read in the accusative, conjoined to the position of مِنْ أَسَاوِرَ. [Translator's note: the source's treatment here appears to assume a genitive reading (وَلُؤْلُؤٍ) for the preceding sentence; it is translated as written.]
It is also said: it is accusative by an omitted verb, its implied form being "and they are given pearls".
Pronouncing the hamza or omitting it are two dialectal forms, both of which have been read.

ukberi-tibyan:24-24.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَهُدُوا إِلَى الطَّيِّبِ مِنَ الْقَوْلِ وَهُدُوا إِلَى صِرَاطِ الْحَمِيدِ (٢٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مِنَ الْقَوْلِ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الطَّيِّب, or from the pronoun in it.

ukberi-tibyan:25-25.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَيَصُدُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ وَالْمَسْجِدِ الْحَرَامِ الَّذِي جَعَلْنَاهُ لِلنَّاسِ سَوَاءً الْعَاكِفُ فِيهِ وَالْبَادِ وَمَنْ يُرِدْ فِيهِ بِإِلْحَادٍ بِظُلْمٍ نُذِقْهُ مِنْ عَذَابٍ أَلِيمٍ (٢٥))
His saying, the Exalted: (وَيَصُدُّونَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent in «كَفَرُوا». It is also said: it is conjoined according to the meaning, since the implied form is "they disbelieve and they bar", or "they disbelieved and they barred"; on these two views the khabar (predicate) is omitted, its implied form being "will be punished", indicated by the end of the verse. It is also said: the wāw is redundant (zāʾida), and it is the khabar.
(جَعَلْنَاهُ): it takes two objects; the pronoun is the first, and concerning the second there are three views. The first: «لِلنَّاسِ»; and His saying, the Exalted, «سَوَاءً» is a fronted khabar, and what follows it is the mubtadaʾ (subject), and the clause is a ḥāl either from the pronoun, namely the hāʾ, or from the pronoun in the preposition (and its genitive noun).
The second view: that «لِلنَّاسِ» is a ḥāl, and the clause after it is in the position of the second object.
The third: that the second object is «سَوَاءً» according to the reading of those who put it in the accusative, and «الْعَاكِفُ» is the fāʿil (agent) of «سَوَاءً».
It is also possible that «جَعَلَ» takes a single object; and «لِلنَّاسِ» is a ḥāl, or an object reached by means of the preposition.
«الْعَاكِفِ» has been read in the genitive, as a badal (substitute) from النَّاس; on this reading «سَوَاءً» is accusative and nothing else.
(مَنْ يُرِدْ): the majority read ḍamma on the yāʾ, from الْإِرَادَة ("wanting").
It is read anomalously (shādhdh) with fatḥa on it (يَرِدْ), from الْوُرُود ("arriving"); on this reading «بِإِلْحَادٍ» is a ḥāl, i.e. "involved in deviation"; while on the first reading the bāʾ is redundant. It is also said: the object is omitted; i.e. "transgression by deviation" (تَعَدِّيًا بِإِلْحَادٍ).
{بِظُلْمٍ}: a badal with repetition of the preposition. It is also said: it too is a ḥāl, i.e. "a wrongful deviation". It is also said: the implied form is "deviation because of wrongdoing".

ukberi-tibyan:26-26.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا لِإِبْرَاهِيمَ مَكَانَ الْبَيْتِ أَنْ لَا تُشْرِكْ بِي شَيْئًا وَطَهِّرْ بَيْتِيَ لِلطَّائِفِينَ وَالْقَائِمِينَ وَالرُّكَّعِ السُّجُودِ (٢٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَإِذْ بَوَّأْنَا): i.e. "mention"; «مَكَانَ الْبَيْتِ» is an adverb (ẓarf); and the lām in لِإِبْرَاهِيمَ is redundant (zāʾida); i.e. "We settled him at the place of the House". The evidence for this is His saying, the Exalted: (وَلَقَدْ بَوَّأْنَا بَنِي إِسْرَائِيلَ). It is also said: the lām is not redundant, and the meaning is "We prepared".
(أَلَّا تُشْرِكْ): its implied form is "saying to him: do not associate"; so أَنْ is explicative (mufassira) of the saying. It is also said: it is maṣdar-forming (maṣdariyya); i.e. "We did that so that you would not associate", the prohibition being made its ṣila; this is strengthened by the reading of those who read it with yāʾ.
(الْقَائِمِينَ): i.e. those who reside. It is also said: He meant those who pray.

ukberi-tibyan:27-27.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَأَذِّنْ فِي النَّاسِ بِالْحَجِّ يَأْتُوكَ رِجَالًا وَعَلَى كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ يَأْتِينَ مِنْ كُلِّ فَجٍّ عَمِيقٍ (٢٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَأَذِّنْ): it is read with the dhāl doubled, undoubled, and with prolongation (وَآذِنْ); i.e. "inform people of the pilgrimage".
(رِجَالًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial); it is the plural of رَاجِل ("one on foot").
It is also read with ḍamma on the rāʾ and undoubled (رُجَالًا); this is rare in plurals.
It is also read with ḍamma and doubling (رُجَّالًا), like صَائِمٌ and صُوَّامٌ. It is also read رُجَالَى, like عُجَالَى.
(وَعَلَى كُلِّ ضَامِرٍ): also in the position of a ḥāl; i.e. "and riding". «ضَامِرٍ» without the (feminine) hāʾ serves for masculine and feminine.
(يَأْتِينَ): construed according to the meaning; the meaning is "and riding on lean camels that come", so it is an adjective (ṣifa) of ضَامِر.
It has been read anomalously (shādhdh) «يَأْتُونَ»; i.e. they come on every lean camel. It is also said: «يَأْتُونَ» is resumptive.
(مِنْ كُلِّ فَجٍّ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to it.

ukberi-tibyan:28-28.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِيَشْهَدُوا مَنَافِعَ لَهُمْ وَيَذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ فِي أَيَّامٍ مَعْلُومَاتٍ).
His saying, the Exalted: (لِيَشْهَدُوا): the lām may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to أَذِّنْ, or attached to يَأْتُوكَ. And Allah knows best.

ukberi-tibyan:3-3.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُجَادِلُ فِي اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَيَتَّبِعُ كُلَّ شَيْطَانٍ مَرِيدٍ (٣)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مَنْ يُجَادِلُ): it is an indefinite noun qualified (by what follows) (nakira mawṣūfa).
(بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ): in the position of the object, or a ḥāl (circumstantial).

ukberi-tibyan:4-4.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (كُتِبَ عَلَيْهِ أَنَّهُ مَنْ تَوَلَّاهُ فَأَنَّهُ يُضِلُّهُ وَيَهْدِيهِ إِلَى عَذَابِ السَّعِيرِ (٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (أَنَّهُ): it, together with what it governs, is in the position of the nominative, governed by كُتِبَ.
It is also read كَتَبَ, with fatḥa; i.e. "Allah wrote", so it is in the position of the accusative.
(مَنْ تَوَلَّاهُ): in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject). «مَنْ» is conditional, and its apodosis (jawāb) is «فَإِنَّهُ» [Translator's note: so written in the source, with kasra]. It may also have the meaning of الَّذِي, with «فَأَنَّهُ» as the khabar (predicate); the fāʾ entered it because of the sense of requital contained in الَّذِي. The second «أَنَّ» has fatḥa because the implied form is "then his case is that he…" (فَشَأْنُهُ أَنَّهُ). There is another discussion on it, the like of which we have mentioned at (أَنَّهُ مَنْ يُحَادِدِ اللَّهَ).
It has also been read with kasra in it (فَإِنَّهُ), construed according to the meaning of "it was said to him".

ukberi-tibyan:5-5.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ إِنْ كُنْتُمْ فِي رَيْبٍ مِنَ الْبَعْثِ فَإِنَّا خَلَقْنَاكُمْ مِنْ تُرَابٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ نُطْفَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ عَلَقَةٍ ثُمَّ مِنْ مُضْغَةٍ مُخَلَّقَةٍ وَغَيْرِ مُخَلَّقَةٍ لِنُبَيِّنَ لَكُمْ وَنُقِرُّ فِي الْأَرْحَامِ مَا نَشَاءُ إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى ثُمَّ نُخْرِجُكُمْ طِفْلًا ثُمَّ لِتَبْلُغُوا أَشُدَّكُمْ وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُتَوَفَّى وَمِنْكُمْ مَنْ يُرَدُّ إِلَى أَرْذَلِ الْعُمُرِ لِكَيْلَا يَعْلَمَ مِنْ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍ شَيْئًا وَتَرَى الْأَرْضَ هَامِدَةً فَإِذَا أَنْزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا الْمَاءَ اهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ وَأَنْبَتَتْ مِنْ كُلِّ زَوْجٍ بَهِيجٍ (٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مِنَ الْبَعْثِ): in the position of the genitive as an adjective (ṣifa) of رَيْب; or attached (mutaʿalliq) to رَيْب.
Al-Ḥasan read: الْبَعَثِ, with fatḥa on the ʿayn; it is a dialectal form.
(وَنُقِرُّ): the majority read it with ḍamma (nominative), as a resumption, since the meaning is not "We created you in order to settle…".
It has also been read in the accusative, as being conjoined in wording. The meaning then differs, because the lām in «لِنُبَيِّنَ» is causal, while the lām implied with نُقِرّ is of outcome (ṣayrūra).
It has also been read with fatḥa on the nūn and ḍamma on the qāf and the rāʾ (نَقُرُّ); i.e. "We make dwell".
(طِفْلًا): a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it is a singular with the meaning of a plural. It is also said: the implied form is "We bring forth each one of you as a child", as Allah the Exalted said: (فَاجْلِدُوهُمْ ثَمَانِينَ), i.e. each one of them.
It is also said: it is originally a maṣdar (verbal noun), and for that reason it was not pluralized. (مِنْ بَعْدِ عِلْمٍ شَيْئًا): has been mentioned in al-Naḥl.
(وَرَبَتْ): without hamza, from رَبَا يَرْبُو, when something increases.
It has also been read with hamza (وَرَبَأَتْ); it is from رَبَأَ لِلْقَوْمِ — that is the lookout (الرَّبِيئَة) — when he climbs onto a high place to watch for them; so the meaning is: it rose up.
(وَأَنْبَتَتْ): i.e. things, or kinds; or "of every delightful pair, a pair"; so the object is omitted. According to al-Akhfash, «مِنْ» is redundant (zāʾida).

ukberi-tibyan:6-6.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ وَأَنَّهُ يُحْيِي الْمَوْتَى وَأَنَّهُ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ (٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (ذَلِكَ): a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ» is the khabar (predicate).
It is also said: the mubtadaʾ is omitted; i.e. "the matter is that". It is also said: it is in the position of the accusative; i.e. "We did that".

ukberi-tibyan:8-9.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ مَنْ يُجَادِلُ فِي اللَّهِ بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ وَلَا هُدًى وَلَا كِتَابٍ مُنِيرٍ (٨) ثَانِيَ عِطْفِهِ لِيُضِلَّ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ لَهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا خِزْيٌ وَنُذِيقُهُ يَوْمَ الْقِيَامَةِ عَذَابَ الْحَرِيقِ (٩)).
His saying, the Exalted: (بِغَيْرِ عِلْمٍ): a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the agent in «يُجَادِلُ».
(ثَانِيَ عِطْفِهِ): also a ḥāl; the construct is not pure (ghayr maḥḍa); i.e. "turning away".
(لِيُضِلَّ): it may be attached (mutaʿalliq) to ثَانِيَ, or to يُجَادِلُ.
(لَهُ فِي الدُّنْيَا): it may be an anticipated ḥāl (muqaddara), or a concurrent one (muqārana), i.e. "deserving"; and it may be resumptive.

ukberi-tibyan:30-30.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ وَمَنْ يُعَظِّمْ حُرُمَاتِ اللَّهِ فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ لَهُ عِنْدَ رَبِّهِ وَأُحِلَّتْ لَكُمُ الْأَنْعَامُ إِلَّا مَا يُتْلَى عَلَيْكُمْ فَاجْتَنِبُوا الرِّجْسَ مِنَ الْأَوْثَانِ وَاجْتَنِبُوا قَوْلَ الزُّورِ (٣٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (ذَلِكَ): i.e. "the matter is that".
(فَهُوَ خَيْرٌ): هُوَ is the pronoun of the honouring (التَّعْظِيم) indicated by يُعَظِّمُ.
(إِلَّا مَا يُتْلَى): the exception may be disconnected (munqaṭiʿ), because there is nothing forbidden among the beasts of livestock; and it may be connected (muttaṣil), being directed to what has been forbidden among them for an incidental reason, such as dying (of itself) and the like.
(مِنَ الْأَوْثَانِ): «مِنْ» is for explaining the genus; i.e. "avoid the filth of this kind"; and here it has the meaning of the beginning of the extent.

ukberi-tibyan:31-31.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (حُنَفَاءَ لِلَّهِ غَيْرَ مُشْرِكِينَ بِهِ وَمَنْ يُشْرِكْ بِاللَّهِ فَكَأَنَّمَا خَرَّ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ فَتَخْطَفُهُ الطَّيْرُ أَوْ تَهْوِي بِهِ الرِّيحُ فِي مَكَانٍ سَحِيقٍ (٣١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (حُنَفَاءَ): it is a ḥāl (circumstantial). «غَيْرَ مُشْرِكِينَ» likewise.
(فَكَأَنَّمَا خَرَّ): i.e. "falls" (يَخِرُّ); that is why His saying, the Exalted, «تَخْطَفُهُ» is conjoined to it. The implied form may also be "and it snatches him" (فَهُوَ يَخْطَفُهُ), so that it is the conjoining of a clause to the first clause. There are readings in it that have been mentioned at the beginning of al-Baqara.

ukberi-tibyan:32-32.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ وَمَنْ يُعَظِّمْ شَعَائِرَ اللَّهِ فَإِنَّهَا مِنْ تَقْوَى الْقُلُوبِ (٣٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (فَإِنَّهَا مِنْ تَقْوَى الْقُلُوبِ): concerning the feminine pronoun there are two views:
The first: it is the pronoun of الشَّعَائِر, and the muḍāf is omitted, its implied form being "then honouring them…"; and the returning pronoun referring to «مَنْ» is omitted, i.e. "then honouring them is of it", or "is of the piety of the hearts on their part". According to the view of the Kufans it may be construed with the implied form "of the piety of their hearts", the alif and lām standing in place of the pronoun.
The second view: that it is the pronoun of a feminine maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "then the reverence", or "the sanctity", or "the trait". The returning pronoun is implied as before.

ukberi-tibyan:33-34.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَكُمْ فِيهَا مَنَافِعُ إِلَى أَجَلٍ مُسَمًّى ثُمَّ مَحِلُّهَا إِلَى الْبَيْتِ الْعَتِيقِ (٣٣) وَلِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ جَعَلْنَا مَنْسَكًا لِيَذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَى مَا رَزَقَهُمْ مِنْ بَهِيمَةِ الْأَنْعَامِ فَإِلَهُكُمْ إِلَهٌ وَاحِدٌ فَلَهُ أَسْلِمُوا وَبَشِّرِ الْمُخْبِتِينَ (٣٤)).
His saying, the Exalted: (لَكُمْ فِيهَا): the pronoun refers to the beasts of livestock.
(الْمَنْسَكُ): it is read with fatḥa on the sīn and with kasra, and they are two dialectal forms. It is also said: fatḥa is for the maṣdar (verbal noun), and kasra for the place.

ukberi-tibyan:35-35.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ وَجِلَتْ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَالصَّابِرِينَ عَلَى مَا أَصَابَهُمْ وَالْمُقِيمِي الصَّلَاةِ وَمِمَّا رَزَقْنَاهُمْ يُنْفِقُونَ (٣٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (الَّذِينَ إِذَا ذُكِرَ اللَّهُ): it may be accusative as an adjective (ṣifa), or a badal (substitute), or by implying أَعْنِي ("I mean"); and it may be nominative by implying «هُمْ» ("they are").
(وَالْمُقِيمِي الصَّلَاةِ): the majority read the genitive by the construct. Al-Ḥasan read it in the accusative (الصَّلَاةَ), the implied form being وَالْمُقِيمِينَ; he dropped the nūn for lightness, not because of the construct.

ukberi-tibyan:36-36.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالْبُدْنَ جَعَلْنَاهَا لَكُمْ مِنْ شَعَائِرِ اللَّهِ لَكُمْ فِيهَا خَيْرٌ فَاذْكُرُوا اسْمَ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهَا صَوَافَّ فَإِذَا وَجَبَتْ جُنُوبُهَا فَكُلُوا مِنْهَا وَأَطْعِمُوا الْقَانِعَ وَالْمُعْتَرَّ كَذَلِكَ سَخَّرْنَاهَا لَكُمْ لَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ (٣٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَالْبُدْنَ): it is the plural of بَدَن, whose singular is بَدَنَة, like خَشَبَة and خَشَب. It is also said: it is the plural of بَدَنَة, like ثَمَرَة and ثَمَر. It is also read with ḍamma on the dāl (الْبُدُنَ), like ثُمُر.
The majority read the accusative, by an omitted verb, i.e. "and We made the sacrificial camels". It is also read in the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
(لَكُمْ): i.e. "for your sake", so it is attached (mutaʿalliq) to the verb.
(مِنْ شَعَائِرِ): the second object.
(لَكُمْ فِيهَا خَيْرٌ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial).
(صَوَافَّ): a ḥāl from the hāʾ; i.e. lined up side by side.
It is also read «صَوَافِنَ», whose singular is صَافِن: one that stands on three legs and on the tip of the hoof of the fourth; and that is when the sacrificial camel is hobbled.
It is also read «صَوَافِيَ», i.e. purely for Allah the Exalted.
It is also read with the yāʾ quiescent (صَوَافِيْ); this is one of the cases of a defective noun (manqūṣ) made quiescent in the accusative position.
(الْقَانِعَ): with the alif, from your saying قَنِعَ بِهِ, when one is content with a small thing.
It is also read without the alif (الْقَنِعَ), from your saying قَنَعَ قُنُوعًا, when one begs.
(الْمُعْتَرَّ): the one who presents himself (asking). It is also read الْمُعْتَرِيَ with fatḥa on the yāʾ, and it has the same meaning; one says عَرَّهُمْ, اعْتَرَّهُمْ, عَرَاهُمْ and اعْتَرَاهُمْ, when he approaches them to ask.
(كَذَلِكَ): the kāf is a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar (verbal noun), its implied form being "We subjected them a subjecting like what we mentioned".

ukberi-tibyan:37-37.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَنْ يَنَالَ اللَّهَ لُحُومُهَا وَلَا دِمَاؤُهَا وَلَكِنْ يَنَالُهُ التَّقْوَى مِنْكُمْ كَذَلِكَ سَخَّرَهَا لَكُمْ لِتُكَبِّرُوا اللَّهَ عَلَى مَا هَدَاكُمْ وَبَشِّرِ الْمُحْسِنِينَ (٣٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (لَنْ يَنَالَ اللَّهَ): the majority read it with yāʾ, because اللُّحُوم and الدِّمَاء are broken plurals, so their femininity is not real, and there is also a separation between the two (the verb and its agent).
It is also read with tāʾ (تَنَالَ); and likewise «يَنَالُهُ التَّقْوَى مِنْكُمْ».

ukberi-tibyan:38-38.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُدَافِعُ عَنِ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَا يُحِبُّ كُلَّ خَوَّانٍ كَفُورٍ (٣٨)).
His saying, the Exalted: (إِنَّ اللَّهَ يُدَافِعُ): it is read without an alif (يَدْفَعُ) and with the alif, and the two are the same.
It is also said: the alif indicates that the mutual repelling takes place between Allah the Exalted and whoever intends harm to the believers.

ukberi-tibyan:39-39.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أُذِنَ لِلَّذِينَ يُقَاتَلُونَ بِأَنَّهُمْ ظُلِمُوا وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ عَلَى نَصْرِهِمْ لَقَدِيرٌ (٣٩)).
His saying, the Exalted: (أُذِنَ): it is read with the agent named (أَذِنَ) and with it unnamed; and likewise «يُقَاتَلُونَ». The implied form is: "permission was given to them to fight because of the injustice directed at them".

ukberi-tibyan:40-40.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا مِنْ دِيَارِهِمْ بِغَيْرِ حَقٍّ إِلَّا أَنْ يَقُولُوا رَبُّنَا اللَّهُ وَلَوْلَا دَفْعُ اللَّهِ النَّاسَ بَعْضَهُمْ بِبَعْضٍ لَهُدِّمَتْ صَوَامِعُ وَبِيَعٌ وَصَلَوَاتٌ وَمَسَاجِدُ يُذْكَرُ فِيهَا اسْمُ اللَّهِ كَثِيرًا وَلَيَنْصُرَنَّ اللَّهُ مَنْ يَنْصُرُهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَقَوِيٌّ عَزِيزٌ (٤٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (الَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا): it is a naʿt (adjective) of the first الَّذِينَ, or a badal (substitute) from it, or in the position of the accusative by أَعْنِي ("I mean"), or in the position of the nominative by implying «هُمْ» ("they are").
(إِلَّا أَنْ يَقُولُوا): this is a disconnected exception (istithnāʾ munqaṭiʿ), its implied form being "except for their saying: our Lord is Allah".
(دَفْعُ اللَّهِ) and دِفَاعُهُ: mentioned in al-Baqara.
(صَلَوَاتٌ): i.e. "and places of prayers".
It is also read with the lām quiescent, with fatḥa on the ṣād and with kasra.
It is also read with ḍamma on the ṣād and the lām, and with ḍamma on the ṣād and fatḥa on the lām, and with the lām quiescent, as the three dialectal forms come in «حُجْرَة».
It is also read: صُلُوتٌ, with ḍamma on the ṣād and the lām, like صَلْب and صُلُوب.
It is also read «صَلْويثا» [Translator's note: so spelled in the source], with fatḥa on the ṣād, the lām quiescent, a yāʾ after the wāw, and a thāʾ dotted with three dots.
It is also read: «صَلُوتَا», with fatḥa on the ṣād and ḍamma on the lām, and it is an Arabic noun. [Translator's note: so in the source; the form is generally regarded as a borrowed (non-Arabic) word, so "Arabic" may be a copyist's error.]
The pronoun in «فِيهَا» refers back to the places mentioned.

ukberi-tibyan:41-44.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الَّذِينَ إِنْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَقَامُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتَوُا الزَّكَاةَ وَأَمَرُوا بِالْمَعْرُوفِ وَنَهَوْا عَنِ الْمُنْكَرِ وَلِلَّهِ عَاقِبَةُ الْأُمُورِ (٤١) وَإِنْ يُكَذِّبُوكَ فَقَدْ كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ وَعَادٌ وَثَمُودُ (٤٢) وَقَوْمُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَقَوْمُ لُوطٍ (٤٣) وَأَصْحَابُ مَدْيَنَ وَكُذِّبَ مُوسَى فَأَمْلَيْتُ لِلْكَافِرِينَ ثُمَّ أَخَذْتُهُمْ فَكَيْفَ كَانَ نَكِيرِ (٤٤))
His saying, the Exalted: (الَّذِينَ إِنْ مَكَّنَّاهُمْ): it is like (الَّذِينَ أُخْرِجُوا).
(نَكِيرِ): a maṣdar (verbal noun) in the place of الْإِنْكَار ("disapproval").

ukberi-tibyan:45-45.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (فَكَأَيِّنْ مِنْ قَرْيَةٍ أَهْلَكْنَاهَا وَهِيَ ظَالِمَةٌ فَهِيَ خَاوِيَةٌ عَلَى عُرُوشِهَا وَبِئْرٍ مُعَطَّلَةٍ وَقَصْرٍ مَشِيدٍ (٤٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (فَكَأَيِّنْ): it may be in the position of the accusative, governed by what «أَهْلَكْنَاهَا» indicates, and it may be in the position of the nominative as a mubtadaʾ (subject).
(أَهْلَكْنَاهَا) and أَهْلَكْتُهَا are the same in meaning.
(بِئْرٍ): conjoined to قَرْيَة.

ukberi-tibyan:46-46.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَفَلَمْ يَسِيرُوا فِي الْأَرْضِ فَتَكُونَ لَهُمْ قُلُوبٌ يَعْقِلُونَ بِهَا أَوْ آذَانٌ يَسْمَعُونَ بِهَا فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَعْمَى الْأَبْصَارُ وَلَكِنْ تَعْمَى الْقُلُوبُ الَّتِي فِي الصُّدُورِ (٤٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (فَإِنَّهَا): the pronoun is of the story (al-qiṣṣa), and the clause after it explains it.
(الَّتِي فِي الصُّدُورِ): an emphasizing adjective (ṣifa muʾakkida).

ukberi-tibyan:51-51.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَالَّذِينَ سَعَوْا فِي آيَاتِنَا مُعَاجِزِينَ أُولَئِكَ أَصْحَابُ الْجَحِيمِ (٥١)).
His saying, the Exalted: (مُعَجِّزِينَ): a ḥāl (circumstantial). It is also read «مُعَاجِزِينَ», with the alif and without doubling, and it has the meaning of the doubled form, like عَاهَدَ and عَهَّدَ. It is also said: عَاجَزَ means "to race (against)", and عَجَّزَ means "to outstrip".

ukberi-tibyan:52-53.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَمَا أَرْسَلْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِكَ مِنْ رَسُولٍ وَلَا نَبِيٍّ إِلَّا إِذَا تَمَنَّى أَلْقَى الشَّيْطَانُ فِي أُمْنِيَّتِهِ فَيَنْسَخُ اللَّهُ مَا يُلْقِي الشَّيْطَانُ ثُمَّ يُحْكِمُ اللَّهُ آيَاتِهِ وَاللَّهُ عَلِيمٌ حَكِيمٌ (٥٢) لِيَجْعَلَ مَا يُلْقِي الشَّيْطَانُ فِتْنَةً لِلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمْ مَرَضٌ وَالْقَاسِيَةِ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَإِنَّ الظَّالِمِينَ لَفِي شِقَاقٍ بَعِيدٍ (٥٣)).
His saying, the Exalted: (إِلَّا إِذَا تَمَنَّى): it is said: it is an exception from a different genus. It is also said: the whole expression is in the position of an adjective (ṣifa) of نَبِيّ.
(الْقَاسِيَةِ): the alif and lām have the meaning of الَّذِي, and the pronoun in «قُلُوبِهِمْ» is the one referring back to it; «قُلُوبُهُمْ» is nominative, governed by the active participle. It was made feminine because, if the verb were in its place, the feminine tāʾ would attach to it. It is conjoined to الَّذِينَ.

ukberi-tibyan:54-55.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَلِيَعْلَمَ الَّذِينَ أُوتُوا الْعِلْمَ أَنَّهُ الْحَقُّ مِنْ رَبِّكَ فَيُؤْمِنُوا بِهِ فَتُخْبِتَ لَهُ قُلُوبُهُمْ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَهَادِي الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا إِلَى صِرَاطٍ مُسْتَقِيمٍ (٥٤) وَلَا يَزَالُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا فِي مِرْيَةٍ مِنْهُ حَتَّى تَأْتِيَهُمُ السَّاعَةُ بَغْتَةً أَوْ يَأْتِيَهُمْ عَذَابُ يَوْمٍ عَقِيمٍ (٥٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (فَيُؤْمِنُوا): it is conjoined to «لِيَعْلَمَ», and likewise «فَتُخْبِتَ».
(لَهَادِي الَّذِينَ): the majority read it with the construct; it is also read لَهَادٍ, with nunation, with «الَّذِينَ» accusative, governed by it.
(فِي مِرْيَةٍ): with kasra and with ḍamma (مُرْيَة), and they are two dialectal forms.

ukberi-tibyan:56-56.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (الْمُلْكُ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِلَّهِ يَحْكُمُ بَيْنَهُمْ فَالَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ فِي جَنَّاتِ النَّعِيمِ (٥٦)).
His saying, the Exalted: (يَوْمَئِذٍ): accusative, governed by His saying «لِلَّهِ»; and «لِلَّهِ» is the khabar (predicate).
(يَحْكُمُ): resumptive; and it may be a ḥāl (circumstantial) from the name of Allah the Exalted, what governs it being the preposition (with its genitive noun).
(وَالَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَكَذَّبُوا بِآيَاتِنَا فَأُولَئِكَ لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ مُهِينٌ (٥٧) وَالَّذِينَ هَاجَرُوا فِي سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ ثُمَّ قُتِلُوا أَوْ مَاتُوا لَيَرْزُقَنَّهُمُ اللَّهُ رِزْقًا حَسَنًا وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَهُوَ خَيْرُ الرَّازِقِينَ (٥٨))
His saying, the Exalted: (فَأُولَئِكَ): the clause is the khabar of الَّذِينَ; the fāʾ entered because of the sense of requital.
(قُتِلُوا): with the tāʾ undoubled and doubled (قُتِّلُوا); and «لَيَرْزُقَنَّهُمُ» is the khabar. «رِزْقًا» is a second object; and it may possibly be an emphasizing maṣdar (verbal noun).

ukberi-tibyan:59-59.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لَيُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ مُدْخَلًا يَرْضَوْنَهُ وَإِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَلِيمٌ حَلِيمٌ (٥٩))
His saying, the Exalted: (لَيُدْخِلَنَّهُمْ): it may be a badal (substitute) from لَيَرْزُقَنَّهُمْ; and it may be resumptive.
(مُدْخَلًا) with ḍamma and with fatḥa (مَدْخَلًا); this has been mentioned in al-Nisāʾ.

ukberi-tibyan:60-60.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ وَمَنْ عَاقَبَ بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبَ بِهِ ثُمَّ بُغِيَ عَلَيْهِ لَيَنْصُرَنَّهُ اللَّهُ إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورٌ (٦٠)).
His saying, the Exalted: (ذَلِكَ): i.e. "the matter is that", and what follows it is resumptive.
(بِمِثْلِ مَا عُوقِبَ بِهِ): the bāʾ in it has the meaning of cause, not the meaning of instrument; and «لَيَنْصُرَنَّهُ» is the khabar (predicate) of مَنْ.

ukberi-tibyan:62-62.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (ذَلِكَ بِأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْحَقُّ وَأَنَّ مَا يَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِهِ هُوَ الْبَاطِلُ وَأَنَّ اللَّهَ هُوَ الْعَلِيُّ الْكَبِيرُ (٦٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (هُوَ الْحَقُّ): «هُوَ» may be a tawkīd (emphasis), a separating pronoun (faṣl), or a mubtadaʾ (subject).
(يَدْعُونَ) with yāʾ and with tāʾ, and the meaning is clear.

ukberi-tibyan:63-63.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ أَنْزَلَ مِنَ السَّمَاءِ مَاءً فَتُصْبِحُ الْأَرْضُ مُخْضَرَّةً إِنَّ اللَّهَ لَطِيفٌ خَبِيرٌ (٦٣))
His saying, the Exalted: (فَتُصْبِحُ الْأَرْضُ): the verb was put in the nominative (indicative) here, even though the form of a question precedes it, for two reasons. First: it is a question with the meaning of a statement, i.e. "you have seen", so it has no answer. Second: what follows the fāʾ is put in the accusative (subjunctive) when what is asked about is a cause of it; but his seeing the sending down of the water does not necessitate the earth's becoming green — that results only from the water. The implied form is "and it", i.e. the situation (al-qiṣṣa), and «تُصْبِحُ» is the khabar (predicate).
It may also be that «فَتُصْبِحُ» has the meaning of أَصْبَحَتْ, conjoined to أَنْزَلَ, so it then has no grammatical position.
(مُخْضَرَّةً): a ḥāl (circumstantial), and it is an active participle.
It has been read anomalously (shādhdh) with fatḥa on the mīm and the ḍād undoubled (مَخْضَرَةً), like مَبْقَلَة and مَجْزَرَة; i.e. possessing greenness.

ukberi-tibyan:65-65.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (أَلَمْ تَرَ أَنَّ اللَّهَ سَخَّرَ لَكُمْ مَا فِي الْأَرْضِ وَالْفُلْكَ تَجْرِي فِي الْبَحْرِ بِأَمْرِهِ وَيُمْسِكُ السَّمَاءَ أَنْ تَقَعَ عَلَى الْأَرْضِ إِلَّا بِإِذْنِهِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ بِالنَّاسِ لَرَءُوفٌ رَحِيمٌ (٦٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَالْفُلْكَ): concerning its accusative there are two views. First: it is accusative, governed by سَخَّرَ, conjoined to «مَا». Second: it is conjoined to the noun of إِنَّ.
(تَجْرِي): a ḥāl (circumstantial) on the first view, and a khabar (predicate) on the second.
It is also read in the nominative (وَالْفُلْكُ), with «تَجْرِي» as the khabar. (أَنْ تَقَعَ): a mafʿūl lahu (object of purpose), i.e. "out of aversion to its falling". It may also be in the position of the genitive, i.e. "from falling".
It is also said: in the position of the accusative as a badal of inclusion (badal al-ishtimāl); i.e. "and He holds back the falling of the sky", i.e. He prevents it.

ukberi-tibyan:67-67.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (لِكُلِّ أُمَّةٍ جَعَلْنَا مَنْسَكًا هُمْ نَاسِكُوهُ فَلَا يُنَازِعُنَّكَ فِي الْأَمْرِ وَادْعُ إِلَى رَبِّكَ إِنَّكَ لَعَلَى هُدًى مُسْتَقِيمٍ (٦٧)).
His saying, the Exalted: (فَلَا يُنَازِعُنَّكَ): it is also read «يَنْزِعُنَّكَ», with fatḥa on the yāʾ, kasra on the zāy and the nūn quiescent; i.e. "let them not draw you out".

ukberi-tibyan:72-72.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَإِذَا تُتْلَى عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتُنَا بَيِّنَاتٍ تَعْرِفُ فِي وُجُوهِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا الْمُنْكَرَ يَكَادُونَ يَسْطُونَ بِالَّذِينَ يَتْلُونَ عَلَيْهِمْ آيَاتِنَا قُلْ أَفَأُنَبِّئُكُمْ بِشَرٍّ مِنْ ذَلِكُمُ النَّارُ وَعَدَهَا اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا وَبِئْسَ الْمَصِيرُ (٧٢)).
His saying, the Exalted: (يَكَادُونَ): the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) from الَّذِينَ, or from الْوُجُوه, because the faces are used to express their owners, as Allah the Exalted said: (وُجُوهٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ عَلَيْهَا غَبَرَةٌ) and then said (أُولَئِكَ هُمُ الْكَفَرَةُ الْفَجَرَةُ).
His saying, the Exalted: (النَّارُ): it is read in the nominative, and there are two views on it. First: it is a mubtadaʾ (subject), and «وَعَدَهَا» is the khabar (predicate). Second: it is the khabar of an omitted mubtadaʾ, i.e. "it is the Fire", i.e. the worse thing; on this view «وَعَدَهَا» is resumptive, since there is nothing in the clause fit to govern a ḥāl.
It is also read in the accusative (النَّارَ), by implying أَعْنِي ("I mean"), or governed by the وَعَدَ indicated by «وَعَدَهَا».
It is also read in the genitive (النَّارِ), as a badal (substitute) from شَرّ.

ukberi-tibyan:73-73.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (يَا أَيُّهَا النَّاسُ ضُرِبَ مَثَلٌ فَاسْتَمِعُوا لَهُ إِنَّ الَّذِينَ تَدْعُونَ مِنْ دُونِ اللَّهِ لَنْ يَخْلُقُوا ذُبَابًا وَلَوِ اجْتَمَعُوا لَهُ وَإِنْ يَسْلُبْهُمُ الذُّبَابُ شَيْئًا لَا يَسْتَنْقِذُوهُ مِنْهُ ضَعُفَ الطَّالِبُ وَالْمَطْلُوبُ (٧٣)).
His saying, the Exalted: (يَسْلُبْهُمُ): it takes two objects, and «شَيْئًا» is the second.

ukberi-tibyan:75-75.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (اللَّهُ يَصْطَفِي مِنَ الْمَلَائِكَةِ رُسُلًا وَمِنَ النَّاسِ إِنَّ اللَّهَ سَمِيعٌ بَصِيرٌ (٧٥)).
His saying, the Exalted: (وَمِنَ النَّاسِ): i.e. "and from among people, messengers".

ukberi-tibyan:78-78.t:
Allah the Exalted said: (وَجَاهِدُوا فِي اللَّهِ حَقَّ جِهَادِهِ هُوَ اجْتَبَاكُمْ وَمَا جَعَلَ عَلَيْكُمْ فِي الدِّينِ مِنْ حَرَجٍ مِلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ إِبْرَاهِيمَ هُوَ سَمَّاكُمُ الْمُسْلِمِينَ مِنْ قَبْلُ وَفِي هَذَا لِيَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ شَهِيدًا عَلَيْكُمْ وَتَكُونُوا شُهَدَاءَ عَلَى النَّاسِ فَأَقِيمُوا الصَّلَاةَ وَآتُوا الزَّكَاةَ وَاعْتَصِمُوا بِاللَّهِ هُوَ مَوْلَاكُمْ فَنِعْمَ الْمَوْلَى وَنِعْمَ النَّصِيرُ (٧٨)).
His saying, the Exalted: (حَقَّ جِهَادِهِ): it is accusative as a maṣdar (verbal noun); and it may be a naʿt (adjective) of an omitted maṣdar, i.e. "a striving that is the true striving for Him".
(مِلَّةَ أَبِيكُمْ): i.e. "follow the creed of your father". It is also said: its implied form is "like the creed of…", because the meaning is "He has made the religion easy for you like the creed of Ibrāhīm"; so the muḍāf was omitted and the muḍāf ilayhi put in its place. (هُوَ سَمَّاكُمُ): it is said: the pronoun refers to Ibrāhīm; on this view His saying «وَفِي هَذَا» means "and in this Qurʾān he named you", i.e. because of it you were named. It is also said: the pronoun refers to Allah the Exalted. (لِيَكُونَ الرَّسُولُ): attached (mutaʿalliq) to سَمَّاكُمْ. And Allah knows best.
